title: After the ad.
description: Spend has a memory. Response has a ceiling. Explore two building blocks of marketing mix models before trusting a budget recommendation.

cases.name: Carryover · one spend pulse
cases.title: The campaign ends. The effect lingers.
cases.context: A single 100-unit spend pulse in week zero. All later spend is zero. Compare three memory rates with a 12-week truncation.
cases.readout: Adstock is the weighted sum of current and preceding spend, using α^lag. This implementation is not normalized: a larger α changes both persistence and total mass.
cases.note: The drop to zero at week 12 is the explicit truncation, not an estimated biological or customer-memory boundary.

cases.context: Two known Hill curves: β=(8,12), K=(12,30), S=2. Allocate a fixed budget between channels; no spend can be negative.
cases.readout: This is a single-period response model. Unlike the carryover scenario, this calculation does not apply adstock. Response is not revenue or profit.

method: Carryover reuses geometric_adstock_np from the existing lab. It computes a finite unnormalized sum of α^lag times spend; a pulse makes its impulse response explicit.
Allocation reuses hill_np: β × x^S/(K^S+x^S). The response parameters are specified, not fitted. Every nonnegative integer split is evaluated, preserving the total budget exactly.
With S=1 each curve is concave; S=2 introduces a threshold. The comparison is deterministic and has no statistical uncertainty bands.
limits: This v1 is a mechanics and allocation explorer. It does not run PyMC, posterior inference, lift calibration, or a head-to-head Meridian comparison.
No real marketing data or validated causal attribution. Known response curves omit parameter uncertainty, costs, interactions and changing markets; do not use the suggested split for real spending.
